==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|eff.}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:der|fr:effectif|:afeq|effect<id:noun>|-ive|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|fr|effectif}}, from {{der|en|la|effectīvus|t=productive; effective}}, from {{m|la|efficiō|t=to make; to bring about}}, equivalent to {{af|en|effect|-ive}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪˈfɛktɪv/|a=non-weak vowel}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-effective.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/əˈfɛktɪv/|a=weak vowel}}
* {{IPA|en|/əˈfektɪv/|a=AU}}
* {{homophones|en|affective|aa=weak vowel}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛktɪv|s=3}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# Having the power to produce a required [[effect]] or effects.
#: {{syn|en|efficacious}}
#: {{ux|en|The pill is an '''effective''' method of birth control.}}
#* {{RQ:Bramah Eyes of Max Carrados|passage="Capital idea; we'll go together and complain: two will be more '''effective'''," suggested Mr. Belting.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2016|author=Justin O. Schmidt|title=The Sting of the Wild|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|isbn=978-1-4214-1928-2|page=102
|passage=Fire ants circumvented the problem of an ineffective sting by having an unusual and highly '''effective''' venom that when daubed or sprayed on other ants penetrates their waxy protective integumental barrier and kills or disables them.}}
# Producing a decided or decisive effect.
#: {{syn|en|telling}}
#: {{ux|en|The president delivered an '''effective''' speech!}}
#* {{RQ:Taylor Holy Living|passage=Whosoever is an '''effective''', real cause of doing his neighbour wrong, is criminal.}}
# Efficient, serviceable, or [[operative]], available for useful work.
#: {{ant|en|nominal}}
#: {{ux|en|How long does it take to make a bunch of civilians an '''effective''' military force?}}
#: {{ux|en|My '''effective''' income after taxes and child support is $500 a month.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''effective''' radiated power is determined by multiplying the transmitter power output with the antenna gain.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''effective''' voltage of an alternating current is 0.7 times its peak voltage.}}
# Actually in effect.
#: {{co|en|'''effective''' immediately}}
#: {{ux|en|The curfew is '''effective''' at midnight.}}
# {{lb|en|geometry|of a [[cycle]] or [[divisor]]}} Having no [[negative]] [[coefficient]]s.
# {{lb|en|algebra|of a [[group action]]}} Such that no group [[element]] acts [[trivially]].
# {{lb|en|physics|for any [[effective theory]]}} [[approximate]]; Not describing the fundamental dynamic changes in some system as they happen.

====Usage notes====
Webster's Revised Unabridged Dictionary from 1913 lists {{m|en|efficient}} and {{m|en|effective}} as synonyms, but all major dictionaries now show that these words now only have different meanings in careful use. Use of both for the other meaning is however widespread enough that Longman's Exam Dictionary, for example, finds it necessary to proscribe the use of one for the other with several examples at each entry and provides the following summary:
* efficient = working quickly and without waste
* effective = having the desired effect

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|military}} a [[soldier]] [[fit]] for [[duty]]
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1876|author=w:Dabney Herndon Maury; [[s:Southern Historical Society Papers/Volume 02/October/Recollections of the Elkhorn Campaign|Southern Historical Society Papers: Volume 2, Number 4]]|journal=Recollections of the Elkhorn Campaign
|passage=The Army of the West reached Corinth sometime after the battle of Shiloh. We were 15,000 '''effectives''', and brought Beauregard's effective force up to 45,000 men.}}
